content.title: About
content.content: Chicken empanada is a traditional Spanish‑Latin American pastry made from a thin dough shell filled with seasoned ground chicken, spices, and sometimes vegetables. The crust is crisp, while the filling is juicy and aromatic, making it a popular snack or light meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Empanadas originated in Spain and quickly spread throughout Latin America, where each region added its own twist.
Chicken in empanadas is often seasoned with paprika, cumin, and garlic, giving it a distinctive flavor.
The dough can be baked or fried; fried empanadas are crunchier, baked ones are less fatty.
In Argentina empanadas are commonly served with chimichurri sauce, while in Chile they are paired with a spicy piri‑piri sauce.
Empanadas are convenient to take on the go, making them a popular street food and travel snack.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Chicken meat supplies niacin, vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Moderate carbohydrate content
items.content: The thin wheat dough contributes a moderate amount of carbs, making the empanada suitable for balanced eating.

items.title: Source of iron and zinc
items.content: Chicken delivers iron and zinc, important for immune function and blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Paprika, garlic and other spices add antioxidant compounds that help protect cells.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: The wheat dough can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten intolerance.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Added salt and soy‑based sauces can raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; ensure the empanada is cooked through.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Fried empanadas are higher in calories due to oil; portion control is advisable for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chicken empanada can be enjoyed hot or warm as a standalone snack, or with chimichurri, salsa, or a yogurt dip. Its handheld shape makes it ideal for picnics and on‑the‑go meals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked empanadas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag; reheat in the oven or microwave until the crust is crisp before serving.
